evals.prompt: Our FieldTwin custom tab loads staged assets and connections with GET {backendUrl}/API/v1.10/{project}/subProject/{subProject}:{stream}/stagedAssets and the same path ending in /connections. For the asset the user picks it then calls GET .../stagedAsset/{id} and shows asset.asset.name and Object.keys(asset.connectionsAsFrom). The tenant is on FieldTwin 9.0 now. Can I just change v1.10 to v2.0 in the base URL? If not, show me what the code should look like.
evals.expected_output: States that a prefix change does not work and why. One GET /API/v2.0/subProjects/{SUBPROJECT:STREAM}?resourceTypes=stagedAssets,connections replaces the list calls, and the single-asset read becomes the same stream GET with resourceIds. The parser reads the envelope by type and then ID and treats a missing type key as an empty result, not an error. asset is now an ID that is resolved through a type map instead of the embedded object the v1.10 single GET returned, and connectionsAsFrom is an array of IDs instead of an {ID: true} map. Backdrop resources arrive in the same maps with isForeign unless no-foreign is sent. The version is chosen in configuration because loaded still reports 1.10 on 9.0, with a way to switch back, and the tenant OpenAPI document is checked.

evals.prompt: This function creates a manifold in the current subproject and returns the new id. It does POST {root}/{project}/subProject/{sp}/stagedAsset with body {asset, name, initialState: {x, y, z, rotation, scale}} and then returns (await res.json()).id. Port it to FieldTwin API v2.0.
evals.expected_output: POST /API/v2.0/subProjects/{SUBPROJECT:STREAM} with {stagedAssets: {items: [{asset, name, x, y, z, rotation, scale}]}}: the transform is flat, x and y are required, and initialState is not sent. The new ID is read from the stagedAssets array of the response, not from an id field. The result is read back with ?resourceTypes=stagedAssets&resourceIds=ID because the response carries IDs only and unknown fields are dropped without an error. A timed-out POST is not retried blindly.

evals.prompt: Our importer creates a well and then its first wellbore: POST SP/well, then POST SP/well/{wellId}/wellBore with {name}. I want this on API v2.0, ideally as a single batch request so the two are created atomically.
evals.expected_output: Explains that one request is not possible here: IDs on the subProjects stream are generated by the server and there are no temporary IDs, so a new parent and its new child take two requests. First POST {wells: {items: [...]}} and read the ID from the wells array, then POST {wellBores: {items: [{well: ID, name}]}}. The parent moves from the path into the body as the required well field. Handles the case where the second request fails after the first has committed, by deleting the well or reporting the partial state.

evals.prompt: A server-side cleanup script with an account API token deletes a scratch subproject and then its project: DELETE /API/v1.10/{project}/subProject/{sp} followed by DELETE /API/v1.10/project/{project}. Migrate it to v2.0.
evals.expected_output: DELETE /API/v2.0/projects/{PROJECT_ID} with {subProjects: [qualified ID]} and then DELETE /API/v2.0/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID} with {projects: [ID]}: each resource is deleted on the stream that owns it, and sending a root to its own stream is refused with 403. The account ID is explicit in the URL and is checked against GET /users/whoami. The two deletes are separate requests in separate streams, in child-before-parent order. The empty 200 body is not parsed as JSON.

evals.prompt: We provision metadata with POST /API/v1.10/metadatadefinition {name, vendorId, type: 'numerical', cost: 0, public: true} and then POST /API/v1.10/metadatumlink to attach it to a layer type with relateToType 'layer' and an order of 3. What is the v2.0 version? I would like one request.
evals.expected_output: One POST /API/v2.0/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID} whose body has metaData first and metaDatumLinks second, because types are processed in key order. type becomes kind. The definition is given a client-chosen id so the link can refer to it in the same request through metaDatum. relateToType uses the plural collection name layers, link IDs are generated by the server, and order cannot be set. A duplicate ID or a second link to the same target answers 409. Fields the v2.0 schema does not list, such as public, are dropped silently, so the body is checked against the OpenAPI document and the result is read back.

evals.prompt: After moving our connection list to v2.0 it returns an empty object and no error. The request is GET /API/v2.0/subProjects/{id}?resourceTypes=connections&merge-foreign=true&includeMetaData=false&visibleOnly=1 with the header include-last-modified: true. The same parameters worked on v1.10. What is wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that in v2.0 every query parameter other than resourceTypes, resourceIds, attributes, at, limit, after and sortOrder is an attribute-value filter, so the leftover v1.10 parameters filter the response down to nothing. Removes them and expresses the intent with the supported mechanisms: the no-foreign and no-metadata headers, and a real attribute filter such as visible=true if wanted. Notes that include-last-modified is ignored because lastModified is always present. Recommends building the query from an explicit list of keys, and mentions that an unknown resource type is rejected with 422.

evals.prompt: Here is everything our integration calls on v1.10 under the subproject path: GET changes, GET connection/{id}/segmentsAboveSurface, GET tags, POST heightSamples and GET geojson. Move all of it to v2.0.
evals.expected_output: Maps heightSamples and geojson directly to /API/v2.0/subProjects/{ID}/heightSamples and /geojson. States that changes, segmentsAboveSurface and tags have no v2.0 equivalent and does not invent endpoints for them. Offers the supported choices for each: keep the call on v1.10, which is served side by side, or use the documented alternative (compare lastModified between reads, compute from the connection's intermediary points, read ?attributes=tags and aggregate). Asks the user to decide and reports which calls stay on v1.10.

evals.prompt: Our offboarding job runs on a server with an account API token and calls DELETE /API/v1.10/user/{id} with the header delete-from-instance: true. Convert it to API v2.0.
evals.expected_output: Flags a behaviour change and does not convert it silently. DELETE /API/v2.0/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID} with {users: [ID]} removes the user from the account and its projects only. The replacement for delete-from-instance is DELETE /API/v2.0/users, which removes the user from every account and project unconditionally, where v1.10 only did so when no other account remained, and which accepts a JWT of an IT admin or super admin only, so the job's API token gets 403. Asks which effect is intended and gives a recommendation.

evals.prompt: Our custom tab builds its API root from loaded.backendUrl and loaded.APIVersion. The tenant was upgraded to FieldTwin 9.0 but we are still calling v1.10. How do we move to v2.0 and still be able to go back if something breaks? Some of our calls are account level, such as listing tags.
evals.expected_output: Explains that loaded still reports 1.10 on 9.0, so v2.0 has to be chosen deliberately through the integration's own configuration, not hard-coded and not read from loaded. Keeps one API root per version from the same trusted backend URL so calls can move incrementally, and makes rollback a configuration switch that is actually exercised. Account-level calls need the account ID in the URL, taken from loaded.account or configuration and checked with GET /users/whoami, since another account gets 403. Tags become GET /API/v2.0/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID}?resourceTypes=tags. The bridge, origin checks and token handling are left unchanged.

evals.prompt: A nightly sync using an account API token renames subprojects and sets vendorAttributes with PATCH /API/v1.10/{project}/subProject/{sp} {name, vendorAttributes}, then uses the returned object to refresh our cache. Port it to v2.0.
evals.expected_output: PATCH /API/v2.0/subProjects/{SUBPROJECT:STREAM} with {subProjects: {[qualified ID]: {name, vendorAttributes, updatedBy}}}. updatedBy is required because an API token is patching more than vendorAttributes; it is the e-mail address of the user making the change, the value v1.10 took as userEmail, and without it the answer is 422. The response is {} rather than the updated object, so the cache is refreshed by reading the subproject back from the stream root and unwrapping it by type and ID, and the body is not assumed to contain the resource. Notes that vendorAttributes: null now clears the attributes and that unknown fields are dropped without an error.
